<section aria-labelledby="i-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="local-grid">
      <div class="prose">
        <span class="eyebrow"><span class="dot"></span> Overview</span>
        <h2 id="i-h">Medicare in Tucson</h2>
        <p>Tucson, the heart of Pima County and Southern Arizona, has a strong Medicare market with several major hospital systems and a robust set of Advantage and Part D plans. Pima Council on Aging provides well-regarded local Medicare counseling for residents across the metro area.</p>
        <h3>Original Medicare or Medicare Advantage?</h3>
        <p>Tucson's mix of large health systems gives Advantage shoppers real network choices, while Original Medicare keeps access open across all of them. <strong>Original Medicare</strong> (Parts A &amp; B) lets you use any provider in the U.S. that accepts Medicare and pairs well with a Medigap supplement and a Part D drug plan for predictable costs. <strong>Medicare Advantage</strong> (Part C) plans bundle your coverage, often add dental, vision and hearing, and may have low or $0 premiums &mdash; but they use local networks, so your Tucson-area doctors and pharmacies need to be in-network.</p>
        <p>Whichever direction fits you best, you can <a href="https://planenroll.com/?purl=Darin-Weidauer" target="_blank" rel="noopener">compare Tucson plans and enroll online</a>, or talk it through first with a free SHIP counselor or licensed agent Darin Weidauer.</p>
      </div>
      <div>
        <div class="costcard"><div class="ch"><h3>2026 quick costs</h3><p>Standard federal amounts</p></div>
          <table><tbody>
            <tr><td>Part B premium</td><td>$202.90/mo</td></tr>
            <tr><td>Part B deductible</td><td>$283</td></tr>
            <tr><td>Part A deductible</td><td>$1,736</td></tr>
            <tr><td>Part D drug cap</td><td>$2,100</td></tr>
            <tr><td>Part A premium (most)</td><td>$0</td></tr>
          </tbody></table>
        </div>
        <p class="costnote">See the <a href="/#costs">full 2026 cost breakdown</a> for Parts A, B, C, D and IRMAA.</p>
      </div>

<section aria-labelledby="e-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="section-head"><span class="eyebrow"><span class="dot"></span> Key dates</span>
      <h2 id="e-h">Medicare enrollment windows</h2>
      <p>These deadlines are the same for everyone in Tucson and across Arizona.</p></div>
    
    <div class="timeline">
      <div class="tl"><div class="when">7 months</div><div>
        <h3>Initial Enrollment Period (IEP)</h3>
        <p>Your first chance to sign up: the 3 months before your 65th-birthday month, the birthday month itself, and the 3 months after. Enrolling in the first three months means coverage can start the month you turn 65.</p>
        <span class="pill">Best time to enroll for most people</span></div></div>
      <div class="tl alt"><div class="when">Oct 15<br>&ndash; Dec 7</div><div>
        <h3>Fall Open Enrollment (AEP)</h3>
        <p>Every autumn, anyone with Medicare can join, switch or drop a Medicare Advantage or Part D drug plan. Changes take effect January 1. Review your plan's Annual Notice of Change each fall &mdash; costs and drug lists shift yearly.</p></div></div>
      <div class="tl alt"><div class="when">Jan 1<br>&ndash; Mar 31</div><div>
        <h3>Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment</h3>
        <p>If you're already in a Medicare Advantage plan, you get one more chance early in the year to switch to a different Advantage plan or return to Original Medicare (and add a drug plan).</p></div></div>
      <div class="tl"><div class="when">Jan 1<br>&ndash; Mar 31</div><div>
        <h3>General Enrollment Period (GEP)</h3>
        <p>For people who missed their Initial Enrollment Period and don't qualify for a special exception. Coverage starts the month after you sign up &mdash; and late penalties may apply.</p>
        <span class="pill">Penalties may apply</span></div></div>
      <div class="tl alt"><div class="when">Varies</div><div>
        <h3>Special Enrollment Period (SEP)</h3>
        <p>Life events can open a no-penalty window &mdash; for example, losing employer coverage when you retire (you generally get 8 months to enroll in Part B), moving out of your plan's area, or qualifying for Extra Help. If you're still working at 65 with good employer coverage, an SEP often lets you delay safely.</p></div></div>
      <div class="tl"><div class="when">6 months</div><div>
        <h3>Medigap Open Enrollment</h3>
        <p>A one-time, 6-month window that begins when you're 65 <em>and</em> enrolled in Part B. During it, insurers can't deny you a Medigap policy or charge more for pre-existing conditions. After it closes, that protection generally goes away.</p>
        <span class="pill">Guaranteed acceptance</span></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
<section id="faq" class="band-cream" aria-labelledby="f-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="section-head"><span class="eyebrow"><span class="dot"></span> Tucson FAQ</span>
      <h2 id="f-h">Common questions in Tucson</h2>
      <p>More answers are on our <a href="/#faq">full Medicare FAQ</a>.</p></div>
    <div class="faq" id="faqList">
      <details class="qa" data-cat="local">
        <summary><button type="button">How do I get free Medicare help in Tucson?<span class="plus" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg></span></button></summary>
        <div class="ans">Two easy options: call Arizona's free SHIP counseling line at <strong>1-800-432-4040</strong>, or reach your local Pima Council on Aging (PCOA), Region Two at <strong>520-790-7262</strong>. These services are free, federally funded, and the counselors don't sell insurance. You can also compare and enroll online anytime, or work with licensed agent Darin Weidauer.</div>
      </details>
      <details class="qa" data-cat="local">
        <summary><button type="button">Which hospitals matter for Medicare plans in Tucson?<span class="plus" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg></span></button></summary>
        <div class="ans">In and around Tucson, major providers include Banner – University Medical Center Tucson, Tucson Medical Center (TMC), Carondelet St. Joseph's, and Northwest Medical Center. With Original Medicare you can use any provider that accepts Medicare; with a Medicare Advantage plan, confirm these systems and your specific doctors are in the plan's network before you enroll.</div>
      </details>
      <details class="qa" data-cat="local">
        <summary><button type="button">When can I enroll in Medicare in Tucson?<span class="plus" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg></span></button></summary>
        <div class="ans">The windows are the same statewide and nationwide: your 7-month Initial Enrollment Period around your 65th birthday, Fall Open Enrollment (Oct 15–Dec 7), the Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period (Jan 1–Mar 31), and Special Enrollment Periods triggered by events like retiring. Use the enrollment-window tool on this page to find your exact dates.</div>
      </details>
      <details class="qa" data-cat="start">
        <summary><button type="button">When am I first eligible for Medicare?<span class="plus" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg></span></button></summary>
        <div class="ans"><p>Most people become eligible at <strong>age 65</strong>. You can also qualify earlier if you've received Social Security Disability benefits for 24 months, or if you have ALS or end-stage renal disease. Your Initial Enrollment Period covers the 7 months around your 65th birthday.</p></div>
      </details>
      <details class="qa" data-cat="start">
        <summary><button type="button">Do I get Medicare automatically?<span class="plus" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg></span></button></summary>
        <div class="ans"><p>If you're <strong>already getting Social Security</strong> before 65, you're usually enrolled in Parts A and B automatically and your card arrives by mail. If you're <strong>not</strong> drawing Social Security yet, you generally have to sign up yourself through the Social Security Administration &mdash; it won't happen on its own.</p></div>
      </details>
      <details class="qa" data-cat="choose">
        <summary><button type="button">What is Medigap and do I need it?<span class="plus" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg></span></button></summary>
        <div class="ans"><p>Medigap (Medicare Supplement) is private insurance that fills the gaps in Original Medicare &mdash; the deductibles and that uncapped 20% coinsurance. It's worth considering if you choose Original Medicare and want protection from large, unpredictable bills. Plans are standardized by letter, so a Plan G from one company covers the same as a Plan G from another; compare on price and service. You don't use Medigap with a Medicare Advantage plan.</p></div>
      </details>
      <details class="qa" data-cat="cost">
        <summary><button type="button">I have limited income &mdash; can I get help paying?<span class="plus" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg></span></button></summary>
        <div class="ans"><p>Yes, and many who qualify never apply. The <strong>Medicare Savings Program</strong> can pay your Part B premium, and <strong>Extra Help</strong> dramatically lowers drug costs. Arizonans with very limited income may also qualify for AHCCCS (Medicaid). A free SHIP counselor at 1-800-432-4040 can screen you for all of these in one call.</p></div>
      </details>
      <details class="qa" data-cat="cost">
        <summary><button type="button">What is the new $2,100 drug cap?<span class="plus" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg></span></button></summary>
        <div class="ans"><p>Starting in 2025 and continuing in 2026, there's an annual cap on what you pay out of pocket for covered prescriptions. In <strong>2026 that cap is $2,100</strong> &mdash; once your covered-drug spending reaches it, you pay $0 for those drugs the rest of the year. You can also use the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan to spread the cost into monthly installments at no extra charge.</p></div>
      </details></div>
  </div>
</section>

## Topic guides
- [2026 Medicare costs](https://www.ecosinsurancesolutions.com/arizona/medicare-costs-arizona): Part A, B, D and the full IRMAA table.
- [Medicare Supplement (Medigap)](https://www.ecosinsurancesolutions.com/arizona/medicare-supplement-arizona): Plan G vs Plan N, the six-month window, snowbird considerations. Arizona has NO Medigap birthday rule.
- [Medicare Part D](https://www.ecosinsurancesolutions.com/arizona/medicare-part-d-arizona): the $2,100 out-of-pocket cap, the permanent late-enrolment penalty, Extra Help, pharmacy access.
- [AHCCCS, ALTCS and Medicare Savings Programs](https://www.ecosinsurancesolutions.com/arizona/arizona-medicaid-ahcccs): Arizona applies NO asset or resource test to QMB, SLMB and QI. ALTCS is an entitlement with no waiting list.
- [Veterans and Medicare](https://www.ecosinsurancesolutions.com/arizona/veterans-medicare-arizona): VA is not creditable coverage for delaying Part B; TRICARE For Life requires Part B.
- [FAQ](https://www.ecosinsurancesolutions.com/arizona/faq): the questions Arizonans ask most.
- [Terms of Use](https://www.ecosinsurancesolutions.com/arizona/terms)

## Arizona-specific facts
- Arizona's Medicaid programme is AHCCCS (Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System); long-term care is ALTCS.
- Arizona applies no asset/resource test to the Medicare Savings Programs; the AHCCCS eligibility chart lists the QMB, SLMB and QI-1 resource limit as not applicable. Only income is measured.
- ALTCS is an entitlement programme with no waiting list, unlike the waiver programmes many states run.
- AHCCCS requires its Complete Care and ALTCS contractors to operate a D-SNP in every service area where they hold a Medicaid contract.
- Arizona does NOT have a Medigap birthday rule. The initial six-month Medigap open enrolment window at 65 is therefore more consequential here.
